html:
The Tsuut'ina Nation is a First Nation of southern Alberta, Canada, with its reserve on the south-west edge of Calgary. Older sources call them Sarcee. They speak an Athabaskan language; their ancestors split from the Dane-zaa, or Beaver, people farther north and moved south onto the plains, probably in the 1700s.

On the plains they became mounted bison hunters, part of the spread of horses on the Plains, and allies of the Blackfoot Confederacy. Smallpox epidemics cut their numbers sharply. In 1877 they signed Treaty 7 with Canada, and in the 1880s settled on their reserve near Calgary, where the city has since grown up to its edge.
